lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.focus: graphing polynomial functions and identifying zeros and end behavior
lessonRef.title: Investigation or close reading: graphing polynomial functions and identifying zeros and end behavior

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: This example shows the kind of reasoning the investigation asks for.

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Talk through what changes and what stays fixed before you answer.

items.prompt: Function f is given in vertex form as f(x) = −(x − 2)² + 4, so it opens downward. Function g is given by a table whose greatest output is 8. Which function has the greater maximum, and by how much?
The function f(x) = (x + 1)² + 10 opens upward. State its minimum value and where it occurs.

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: A polynomial has degree 4 and leading coefficient -2. Describe its end behaviour.
choices: the left end falls and the right end rises
the left end rises and the right end falls

items.prompt: For f(x) = (x − 1) / (x + 7), state the vertical asymptote and the horizontal asymptote.
Function f is given in vertex form as f(x) = −3(x + 1)² + 4, so it opens downward. Function g is given by a table whose greatest output is 7. Which function has the greater maximum, and by how much?
The function f(x) = (x − 7)² + 7 opens upward. State its minimum value and where it occurs.

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Write out the reasoning in full sentences. A correct answer with no justification does not count here.

items.prompt: A polynomial has degree 5 and leading coefficient -1. Describe its end behaviour.
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: For f(x) = (x − 4) / (x − 1), state the vertical asymptote and the horizontal asymptote.
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
